title: Observability handoffs and canary rotation logistics (draft)
content:
Purpose:
This doc captures a pragmatic, lightweight protocol for rotating canary stewards, executing observability handoffs, and running the communication/escalation cadence for cross-functional canary and A/B rollouts. It is intentionally operational (checklists, scripts, calendar templates) and focused on human coordination rather than the instrumentation specifics.

Scope and audience:
- Audience: product owners, rollout stewards, SREs, serving-runtime leads, oncall engineers, solutions/SEs involved in customer-facing experiments.
- Scope: internal canaries, progressive rollouts (hosted + dedicated), short-lived A/B slices. Not for multi-month platform migrations (separate process).

High-level goals:
1) Minimize friction when ownership changes during a long canary (clear handoff artifacts).
2) Ensure fast, consistent escalation & rollback decisions (templates + guardrails).
3) Give stewards a predictable, low-noise monitoring view they can trust.

Definitions (working):
- Steward: rotating role (typically 24-72h) that owns the canary window operationally.
- Stewardship window: contiguous time block when a named steward owns the canary.
- Canary slice: traffic cohort (by region, user segment, or endpoint) receiving the experimental variant.
- Critical signal: metric that, when outside threshold, triggers immediate investigation/escalation.

Rotation calendar pattern (recommended):
- Default window: 48 hours for product teams, 72 hours for platform-wide canaries.
- Handoff overlap: 30 minutes overlap for verbal/Slack sync before new steward takes ownership.
- Shadow steward: optional observer from SRE/product for first rotation after a config/infra change.

Template rotation calendar (copy to Google Calendar):
- Day 0 09:00-09:30 — Handoff sync (outgoing -> incoming).
- Day 0 09:30-18:00 — Incoming steward primary.
- Day 1 09:00-17:00 — Incoming steward continues. Handoff prep 16:30-17:00.
- Day 2 09:00-09:30 — Final debrief if rolling off earlier.

Responsibilities (short):
- Steward:
  * Confirm instrumentation dashboards/readouts load in under 30s.
  * Run synthetic smoke checks for key routes.
  * Monitor critical signals and decide on immediate rollback if threshold met.
  * Notify stakeholders on any deviation and file incident if needed.
- Outgoing steward:
  * Summarize recent anomalies (one-paragraph).
  * Attach links to console dashboards, logs, and recent traces.
- SRE on-call:
  * Assist with escalation, execute hotfix or capacity adjustments.
- Product owner:
  * Decide whether to continue experiment after steward flags.

Critical signals and first-tier thresholds (example values — tune per product):
- model_inference_p95_ms > baseline_p95 * 1.5 for 5m -> alarm
- error_rate_5m > baseline_error_5m + 0.5 percentage pts -> alarm
- token_consumption_spike > 2x expected spike for 10m -> investigate cost/regression
- moderation_flag_rate > 0.1% of completions in 10m -> urgent review (safety)
- user-facing-drop (DAU_slice_drop_1h) > 3% -> revert slice

Observability readout (must-have widgets):
- Small single-pane steward dashboard (only essentials):
  * P95 latency (model + request path)
  * Request QPS / concurrency heatmap
  * Error rate (4xx/5xx split)
  * Moderation/TOX flags by category (safety)
  * Model output quality quick-check (sampling of 5 completions/min with heuristics)
  * Cost burn rate (per-variant)
- Link to full troubleshooting dashboard with traces and logs.

Checklist: Starting a new steward window
- [ ] Outgoing steward posts 3-line summary to #rollouts (who, what, known mitigations).
- [ ] Run synthetic baseline: run 10 canonical prompts, confirm response time & content sanity.
- [ ] Confirm steering dashboard refresh and pinned alerts enabled.
- [ ] Incoming steward acknowledges and performs quick readout.

Checklist: If a critical signal triggers
- [ ] Steward triages immediately (5m): check synthetic tests, logs, recent deploys.
- [ ] If transient/no clear cause: scale observation window to 15m, notify product lead.
- [ ] If reproducible or severe: escalate to SRE oncall and product (Slack + page).
- [ ] If severity >= customer-impacting (per SLA): rollback variant and open incident.

Escalation levels and scripts (copy+paste):
- Level 1 (steward only):
  Slack: "@channel Canary steward update: p95 latency on slice X rose to 3.2s (baseline 1.2s). Investigating synthetic runs and recent deploys. Will update in 10m. -- Maya"
- Level 2 (product + SRE oncall):
  Slack/pager: "Paging SRE-oncall: Canary slice X experiencing sustained p95 latency 2.7-3.5s for 15m and error_rate 1.8%. Steward (Maya) requests immediate assistance to triage and consider rollback. Jira: JIRA-RDW-3241"
- Level 3 (exec + customers):
  Email template: Subject: Urgent: Canary rollback for <feature> — short summary, impact, mitigation, ETA to restore. Body: one paragraph summary + open incident link + customer list + owner contact.

Quick rollback decision rubric (thumb rules):
- Immediate rollback if any of: moderation_flag_rate breach, user-facing drop > 3%, or error rate > 2x baseline for 15m.
- Consider pause/slice-reduction if latency degradation without errors but cost spike > 2x.
- For ambiguous regressions (quality of output): pause traffic and run expanded eval set; escalate to PO.

Communication templates (Slack threads / short):
- Steward start post (example): "Steward-up: Maya is steward for canary slice X from 2026-02-14 09:00 UTC -> 2026-02-16 09:00 UTC. Dashboards: <link>. Will post hourly light updates or when signals exceed thresholds."
- Steward hourly update (example): "H1: p95 1.1s (-), errors 0.2% (-), moderation 0.02% (-). No action."
- Steward departure handoff (example): "Handing off: summary=none, open issues=none, recommends=continue 48h. Incoming: @Ethan will take next window."

A/B-specific notes (short):
- A/B slices should carry the same stewarding pattern as canaries if they impact production routing.
- Variant tagging: each variant must have a unique experiment id in telemetry (exp_id) and cost ledger tag to allow per-variant cost signals.
- Gating metric: primary metric must be decided and instrumented before rollout (e.g., conversion rate or answer-quality score).

Post-rollout/rotation artifacts (must produce before leaving team):
- Short debrief note (2–4 bullets): what changed, anomalies, whether rollback/pause occurred, follow-ups.
- Link to saved dashboard and a 5-sample transcript log for quality review.
- If any incidents opened, link to incident commander notes.

Open questions / TODOs (notes to self):
- TODO: automate steward calendar creation and add recurring reminders for overlap syncs.
- Question: should shadow steward be mandatory for experiments that touch security/moderation? (safety team input needed)
- TODO: define minimum synthetic prompt set per product (start with 6 prompts per endpoint).
- TODO: create compact mobile-friendly steward dashboard.

Known limitations and tradeoffs:
- Short stewardship windows mean more rotations (coordination overhead). Longer windows reduce context switching but risk stale owner availability.
- This doc deliberately leaves thresholds generic — teams must tune to product baselines.

Appendix: example quick triage steps (first 15 minutes)
1) Confirm alert validity: run 5 synthetic prompts, check logs for spikes or malformed requests.
2) Check recent deploys (platform + model variants).
3) Check capacity: GPU queue depth, autoscaler events.
4) Sample model outputs (5-10). If quality anomalies, tag artifacts and pause slice.
5) If no immediate root cause: escalate to SRE and extend observation.

Notes & references:
- See linked Confluence for canonical dashboard queries.
- Related: canary-runbook, rollout-contract-template (links in linked_artifacts).

Last quick reminder: this is an operational draft — aim to iterate via actual steward rotations (we will refine templates after 3 live cycles).
